sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Henderson County
sections.html:
The work is split between an Assessor, who sets values, and a Tax Collector, who bills and collects. The collector's counter is Suite 66 on the ground floor at 200 North Grove Street, Hendersonville, NC 28792, open weekdays from 8:30 to 5:00.

Call 828-697-4667 for an appraisal or appeal and 828-697-5595 for payments. The Assessor does not choose rates. The commissioners and the governing boards of Hendersonville, Fletcher, Saluda, Mills River, Flat Rock and Laurel Park each set their own to match their budgets.

One collector bills for the county, thirteen fire districts, Hendersonville, Laurel Park and the Henderson County portion of Saluda. There are 22 tax districts in all, counting the general county district, and rates differ with the services each provides.

For context on pricing, the county had 122,375 people in July 2025, owner-occupied homes with a median value of $351,400, 75.0% owner occupancy and 1,093 building permits issued in 2025. About 29.1% of residents are 65 or over.

All taxable property is valued at 100% of market value under the uniform standards in G.S. 105-283. That covers about 71,500 parcels, some 4,500 businesses with personal property, over 10,000 manufactured homes and more than 100,000 registered vehicles billed monthly.

Henderson reappraises every four years instead of waiting for the eight-year state limit in G.S. 105-286. The last reappraisal was in 2023, and the next takes effect January 1, 2027. A building still under construction on January 1 is valued by its percent complete, and a farm or forest tract in the Present-Use Value Program is assessed below market.

Property tax is expected to pay for about 50% of county operating spending in fiscal year 2027.

Henderson's schedule runs from the January 1, 2027 effective date through tax bills in August 2027. Notices of assessed value should go out around February 1, 2027, so owners see new numbers before the appeal window closes.

Henderson County 2027 reappraisal schedule
DateStep
January 1, 2027Reappraisal effective date
About February 1, 2027Notices of assessed value mailed
January 1 to April 13, 2027Informal appeals to the Assessor
April 14, 2027County review board convenes
May 14, 2027Board adjourns, closing the appeal period
By June 30, 2027Commissioners set the 2027-2028 tax rate
August 2027Tax bills mailed

If you plan to list in 2027, expect the new value to be public before buyers start asking about taxes.

Start with an informal written appeal to the Assessor on the county's standard form. A formal appeal goes to the county review board only if that fails to settle the value, and it must be received before the board adjourns.

  • Once a formal appeal is in, an appraiser meets you to discuss the value and check the information you supplied.
  • If you still disagree, each side presents at a public hearing.
  • The board mails its decision within 30 days of that hearing.
  • The next step is the state Property Tax Commission. Notice is due 30 days from the board's letter, and most cases are heard in Raleigh.

The statewide rules are in G.S. 105-322. Strong exhibits for a seller include recent sales of similar homes nearby, an appraisal tied to a sale contract, and repair quotes for defects a mass appraisal cannot see.

You can mail a check, visit the counter, pay online or use the automated phone line. The counter takes cash, check, money order and cards. A drop box in the south parking lot is emptied daily, and it is no place for cash.

  • Card and e-check payers owe a convenience fee that goes to the payment vendor.
  • Prepayments taken January through July show up as a credit once the bill is issued.
  • If you expect to be late, call before the account is delinquent. Most owners are offered a plan.
  • Mail checks to Henderson County Tax Collector, 200 N Grove St, Ste 66, Hendersonville, NC 28792.

Under G.S. 105-360, taxes are due September 1, paid at par through January 6, and carry interest after that.

With 29.1% of the county 65 or over, the age-based programs reach many owners. The Assessor handles the elderly or permanently disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion, present-use value and the circuit-breaker deferral.

  • Elderly or disabled: $25,000 or half the value of the permanent residence, whichever is greater, if 2026 income is within $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran: $45,000 off appraised value, with no age or income cap.
  • Circuit breaker: tax held to 4.0% of income, or 5.0% above the $38,800 mark up to $58,200, with the excess deferred.

An owner can use only one of the three. Apply on Form AV-9, which the county accepts through June 1 before the tax year. A circuit-breaker deferral is payable when the home transfers.

The Tax Collector may foreclose on real property with delinquent taxes. Sales are held on the courthouse steps at 200 North Grove Street. The county lists each parcel with an estimated opening bid that leaves out interest and expenses accruing daily. Ask the Clerk of Court at 828-694-4100 for upset bid amounts, and call 828-698-3090 with sale questions.

A recent county sale listed 15 parcels with estimated opening bids from $739.08 up to $14,077.24.

A seller with a balance can clear it at closing instead. Get the payoff from the Tax Collector. The seller also pays the deed excise tax of $1.00 per $500 separately.

Here is how a sale with taxes owed usually goes. Request the payoff from the Tax Collector, give it to your closing attorney, and have it paid from your proceeds so the parcel is clear when the deed is recorded. A cash buyer can close on that timeline without waiting for a lender appraisal, though the tax payoff is still settled at closing. If you cannot sell fast enough, call the collector before delinquency to ask about a plan.

sections.h2: Preparing to list in a reappraisal year
sections.html:
Sellers listing around the 2027 reappraisal have a few things to line up. When the notice of assessed value arrives, compare it with recent sales of similar homes nearby. If it looks high, file the informal written appeal before April 14, 2027, since that is when the review board convenes. Hold on to any appraisal tied to a sale contract, and get repair quotes for defects the county could not see from the street.

Remember that the value and the rate are separate. Your appeal changes the value only. The commissioners and your town set the rate by June 30, 2027, and bills follow in August 2027. If a closing falls before then, ask the closing attorney how the year's tax will be prorated and paid.

faqs.q: When is the Henderson County reappraisal effective?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027. The county follows a four-year cycle and last reappraised in 2023, so values reset to market as of that date.

faqs.q: By when must a 2027 value be contested?
faqs.a: The review board adjourns on May 14, 2027, which closes the 2027 appeal period. Informal appeals to the Assessor run from January 1 to April 13, 2027.

faqs.q: Can I pay Henderson County property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes. The Tax Collector encourages monthly installments, accepts prepayments from January through July, and usually offers a payment plan if you call before the bill is delinquent.

faqs.q: Where are tax foreclosure sales held?
faqs.a: On the courthouse steps at 200 North Grove Street, Hendersonville. The Tax Collector lists each parcel with an estimated opening bid, and the Clerk of Court gives current upset bid amounts.

faqs.q: Who sets the Henderson County tax rate?
faqs.a: The Board of Commissioners sets the county rate, and each municipality sets its own. The Assessor only determines value, so an appeal changes the value and not the rate.
